items.title: Albert "June" Gardner Interview, 1996-04-17
items.q: I came up with this, you know, like Jack the Cat.

ctx.x: How important was the radio? Did you listen to radio a lot as a kid?

Yeah, well, I came up with this, you know, like Jack the Cat. These guys used to play, this was before W-Y-L, D-W-M-R-Y, all the so-called black stations came on there. You had, it was limited, and it was rhythm and blues. Yeah. It wasn't rock and roll, you know, so it was limited. But you would catch some of the music that would play the rhythm and blues. But then I lived across the street from some juke joints, and all night long they played the blues. I could hear T-Bone Walker, Lil Green, Blue Lou Barker from…
What about phonograph records? Did you have a, was there a phonograph in your house?
